newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Hoyts would look at UA int'l units.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Hoyts would look at UA int'l units.

text.p: Cinema operator Hoyts Cinemas Ltd said on Wednesday it would look at the international operations of U.S. cinema operator United Artists Theatre Circuit if they became available.

"If United Artists were in a position where they formally looked to sell some parts of their businesses, then if they declare that publicly and, they haven't, then we would look at it," Hoyts chief executive Peter Ivany told reporters.
United Artists owners, Merrill Lynch Capital Partners Inc and Tele-Communications Inc, have not said the company or any of its businesses are for sale.

"Our financial structure is amongst the top in the industry and we have the flexibility to be able to take up opportunities as they come along," Ivany told reporters after the cinema group posted a net profit of A$13.1 million net profit in the six months ended December 31, 1996.
United Artists Theatre Circuits recorded losses in the 1994 and 1995 years and in 1996 it suffered a ratings downgrade by Standard and Poor's on its US$125 million secured notes.
United Artists has 2,300 movies screens across the United States and its international operations include Mexico, where Hoyts also has operations.
